report.title: Global habitat project report, 6 November 2026
report.caveat: Report-derived, now checked: all 12 benchmark configurations and the NEON 2025 diagnostic were reproduced on the frozen folds on 19 November, five global maps were rebuilt, and all twelve original surfaces were recovered north of about 6° S (see the themes section). The coverage figures below are still the report’s.
cohort: 625 iNaturalist positives, 114 Austrian survey-positive locations, 862 other-Culicidae background locations. Background is not confirmed absence.
3 outer spatial folds × seeds 42/202 (≈150 km blocks, ≥20 km separation), 3 inner folds, 12 configurations.
24 score rasters and 6 quality layers over 2,913 processed tiles. Only AlphaEarth was deployed globally among five encoders.
neon: 389 locations, 43 detected, 45 site clusters; 2024 features vs 2025 detections; >10 km from development candidates. A reused diagnostic, not a blind test.
Numerically highest on this diagnostic, but choosing it after inspecting NEON would invalidate a blind-selection claim.
notes: AP measures ranking under the sampling design: 0.8111 is not 81% global accuracy, occupancy or abundance.
Near-ties among the top models do not establish superiority.
Development prevalence (46.16%) and NEON prevalence (11.05%) differ, so APs cannot be subtracted to measure a loss of accuracy.
Bootstrap intervals condition on trained models and omit training, selection and multiple-comparison uncertainty.
An earlier 1,296-site cohort with a different recipe (environment + AE + RF, AP 0.8276) must not be combined with these rankings.
Map disagreement is not a confidence interval; missing cells are not low risk.

figures: sites, 2024 Ae. albopictus cohort
739 presences (625 iNaturalist, 114 Austrian survey detections) vs 862 other-Culicidae background. Recovered from the project Drive; background is not confirmed absence.
held-out fits completed
39 configurations on spatial blocks plus 21 on each transfer design; no failed or skipped fold. Each fit tuned on inner buffered folds only.
best spatial-block AP, a near-tie
Climate 19 + AlphaEarth and AlphaEarth alone with logistic (0.810, 0.808). 21 of 39 configurations lie within 0.02 of the best, all containing AlphaEarth; prevalence 46%.
AUC on the Austrian survey
Best transfer to 313 independent survey sites (36% detected), from climate or fusion with tree learners; AlphaEarth alone reached 0.59–0.65.

findings.head: The report's ranking holds on new folds.
findings.body: On new 150 km EPSG:6933 blocks, AlphaEarth + logistic scored AP 0.808 (report 0.811), fusion + logistic 0.802 (0.810), Environment 41 + RF 0.787 (0.792) and Climate 19 + logistic 0.613 (0.594). Every logistic, RF and BRT cell is within 0.02 of the report. MaxEnt cells differ more because the implementation differs (see caveats).

findings.head: The embedding gain depends on the learner.
findings.body: Adding AlphaEarth to Environment 41 raises a logistic model's AP by +0.104 (95% interval +0.063 to +0.151, better in 6 of 6 folds), but a random forest's by only +0.012 (−0.005 to +0.031) and BRT's by +0.019 (+0.001 to +0.040). Trees recover most of what the embedding adds to a linear model from the explicit variables.

findings.head: Fusion does not beat AlphaEarth alone.
findings.body: Environment + AlphaEarth vs AlphaEarth alone: ΔAP −0.008 (logistic), +0.005 (RF), +0.001 (BRT); every interval includes zero. Equal-score late fusion trails early fusion by 0.014 (−0.033 to +0.003).

findings.head: Inside the fusion, the explicit groups are redundant.
findings.body: Removing any one of climate, ERA5 weather, terrain, land/vegetation or human footprint changes fusion AP by at most 0.008; no removal hurts with an interval excluding zero. Removing AlphaEarth costs 0.104 with logistic but 0.012 with RF (−0.031 to +0.005). Climate 19 + AlphaEarth matches the full 105-feature fusion.

findings.head: Spatial-block scores overstate transfer.
findings.body: Holding out a whole region lowers AUC for every model. Europe is hardest: AlphaEarth alone falls to AUC 0.66–0.69 with logistic, RF or BRT when trained mostly on the Americas, while Environment 41 + RF holds 0.77 and Environment + AlphaEarth PCA-16 + RF 0.81. The Asia-Pacific holdout (156 sites) scores high but is small.

findings.head: On independent survey data, embeddings show no demonstrated gain.
findings.body: Trained without any Austrian rows and tested on 313 AGES survey sites (detected vs not detected), the best AUC came from Climate 19 + BRT (0.765), fusion + BRT (0.755) and Environment 41 + BRT (0.755). AlphaEarth alone reached 0.59–0.65 across the four learners. Fusion minus Environment 41 intervals all include zero (37 clusters). Here RF beat logistic on the fusion by +0.173 AP (+0.044 to +0.270).

findings.head: Most robust across all three designs: trees on explicit features plus a compressed embedding.
findings.body: Environment 41 + train-fold AlphaEarth PCA-16 + RF had the highest mean AUC across spatial, region and survey designs (0.863, 0.839, 0.739). Fusion + BRT had the best worst case (0.755). These are the strongest combinations on held-out data; their margins over Environment 41 + RF are small and not separately tested.

findings.head: MaxEnt (elapid) is not competitive here.
findings.body: On Environment 41 it trails RF by 0.090 AP (−0.128 to −0.045, 0 of 6 folds better) and ties logistic regression. It falls below the report's R MaxNet value (0.773), so this result should not replace the report's MaxNet cells.

caveats: The 18 November section uses new 150 km blocks and a pre-amendment snapshot; the exact-fold reproduction and new 19 November experiments are in the next section and agree with it.
AP ranks presences above other-Culicidae background under this sampling design. It is not accuracy, occupancy or abundance, and AP values from designs with different prevalence cannot be subtracted.

Intervals are paired block-cluster bootstraps on fixed out-of-fold predictions. They omit training, tuning and multiple-comparison uncertainty; about 40 pairs were tested, so treat single borderline intervals with care.
Human footprint alone (4 variables) reaches AP 0.67 on spatial blocks, which points to reporting bias in presence/background labels. Embeddings can encode the same signal.
The Austrian survey set is one country, one year and 37 spatial clusters. It tests transfer to a different endpoint, not global accuracy.
No temporal holdout was possible: every cohort row and feature is from 2024. NEON 2025 features were not in the uploaded archives.
not_run: Original maps south of about 6° S.

Parts 18–21 of the Drive archive (06 derived_global_mapping_2024) are not uploaded yet; north of 6° S the original 12 surfaces are recovered from the deployment tiles. Rebuilding Environment 41 from scratch needs Earth Engine.
A 500 m global extraction is about 8 million circles; the overview approximation agrees with point predictions (Spearman 0.93 logistic, 0.88 RF) but is not the original surface.
Sentinel-2 chips use the scene classification mask from Earth Search; 30 of 1,601 sites had no clear 2024 observation and are excluded from encoder and S2 arms.
The public mirror covers 1,975 of 2,462 locations for 2025.
The shared folder is readable by link again, and the integrated-feature archives and NEON token were taken from it; the Google Drive connector itself still needs re-authorising.
Dryad now needs an account token; the Kraemer compendium was taken from its CC0 Zenodo mirror instead (MD5 identical).

Protocol: 150 km EPSG:6933 blocks; 3 outer × 3 inner GroupKFold; 20 km train–test buffer; seeds 42 and 202; inner-fold AP selects C (0.1, 1), min_samples_leaf (3, 12), L2 (1, 10) or MaxEnt β (1, 2). Scaling and PCA are fitted inside training folds.

figures: fold × model jobs verified exactly
The report's AP recomputed from its own stored out-of-fold predictions on the frozen folds: maximum difference 0.0, including the two R MaxNet configurations.
mean-AP gap after refitting
Logistic, RF and BRT retrained here on the frozen folds reproduce all 10 configurations' mean AP within 0.006 (logistic per-site score correlation ≥ 0.998).
TESSERA 128 vs AlphaEarth 64, ΔAP
Logistic head on the frozen folds; 95% interval −0.043 to +0.035. Both embeddings rank habitat equally well.
NEON 2025 AP: best vs selected
Climate 19 + RF vs the report's development winner (AlphaEarth + logistic, which ranks 11th of 19) on 389 independent 2025 sites, 11% detected.

findings.head: The report is reproduced on its own folds.
findings.body: All 72 fold × model results recompute exactly from the original stored predictions, and refitting logistic, RF and BRT here on the frozen folds reproduces every configuration's mean AP within 0.006. The development winner, AlphaEarth + logistic (AP 0.811), is confirmed. So is the NEON 2025 diagnostic (AP 0.344; report 0.3445) and its fusion − environment logistic gain (+0.202, 95% interval +0.035 to +0.399; report +0.196).

findings.head: TESSERA matches AlphaEarth, not more.
findings.body: TESSERA 128 + logistic reaches AP 0.802 against AlphaEarth's 0.812: ΔAP +0.004 (−0.043 to +0.035), better in 2 of 6 folds. An equal-dimension TESSERA PCA-64 also ties. Compressing TESSERA to 32 dimensions costs 0.023 (−0.044 to −0.006). Stacking both embeddings adds +0.010 (−0.017 to +0.031). Either embedding lifts a logistic model about +0.11 over Environment 41.

findings.head: MLPs replicate; nonlinear late fusion is unstable.
findings.body: Over 10 seeds, the AlphaEarth, Environment 41 and early-fusion MLPs bracket the report's values (for example AlphaEarth 0.800–0.819 vs 0.810). Stacked nonlinear late fusion ranges 0.550–0.795 (mean 0.688), so the report's 0.786 was a favourable seed, not a reliable gain.

findings.head: Across years, development rank does not carry over.
findings.body: Trained on 2024 and scored on 2025 NEON traps (389 sites ≥ 10 km from training), the best AP came from Climate 19 + RF (0.477) and Environment + TESSERA logistic (0.453). The selected AlphaEarth + logistic ranked 11th of 19 (0.344). Embeddings help linear models here (adding TESSERA to Environment 41: +0.238, +0.041 to +0.381) but not random forests.

findings.head: In Austria 2025, climate-only trees transfer best.
findings.body: Without any Austrian training rows, Climate 19 + BRT (AP 0.744) and + RF (0.725) beat every embedding model (0.45–0.67) on 203 Austrian 2025 sites (37% detected). With the same traps' 2024 records in training, RF on any representation reaches about 0.80. That gain is site persistence, not transfer.

findings.head: Supported conclusion.
findings.body: Satellite embeddings are the strongest single representation for ranking held-out spatial blocks within the 2024 development distribution, and AlphaEarth and TESSERA are interchangeable there. Across years and new monitoring networks, climate-driven tree models are more reliable, and no embedding shows a demonstrated advantage over them. Embedding gains are therefore a hypothesis for transfer, not a demonstrated improvement.

Frozen Prithvi-EO-2.0, Clay v1.5, CROMA and SatMAE on 2024 Sentinel-2 chips, logistic head, 1,555 sites; every interval excludes 0.

findings.head: MaxNet now refits exactly, and transfers well.
findings.body: The official R maxnet (default features, cloglog) reproduces Climate 19 MaxNet 0.6770 and Environment 41 MaxNet 0.7729 to every fold. On NEON 2025, R MaxNet on Climate 19 reaches AP 0.481, tied with the best model (Climate 19 + RF, 0.477). The Python elapid stand-in had given 0.368, so earlier MaxEnt transfer results understated it.

findings.head: Support size and grid do not matter between 250 m and 1 km.
findings.body: AlphaEarth re-extracted from the native 10 m layer gives AP 0.808 at 250 m, 0.811 at 500 m and 0.812 at 1 km; the single point pixel is lower (0.789; −0.023, −0.053 to +0.007). Native extraction equals the original 250 m working-grid features (+0.0003, −0.004 to +0.004).

findings.head: AlphaEarth beats raw spectra and four open encoders.
findings.body: Quarterly Sentinel-2 statistics with seasonal dynamics reach AP 0.632 with a logistic head, 0.186 below AlphaEarth (−0.256 to −0.116). Frozen Prithvi, Clay, CROMA and SatMAE embeddings of the same 1.44 km chips score 0.646–0.684, all 0.11–0.16 below AlphaEarth. Pretraining helps (+0.03 to +0.07 over random weights; the Prithvi and CROMA intervals exclude 0), and Clay’s time and location metadata add nothing (+0.004). Adding any of them to AlphaEarth lowers AP by 0.04–0.10.

findings.head: Location stands in for missing nonlinearity, and human features carry sampling signal.
findings.body: Coordinates alone reach AP 0.709 with RF (−0.097 vs Environment 41 RF) and add nothing to AlphaEarth (+0.003). SatCLIP lifts a logistic Environment 41 by +0.089 (+0.033 to +0.151) but not past AlphaEarth. Dropping the four human-activity features costs little (−0.009 logistic, −0.004 RF). Fixing them at the training median, as a bias covariate, costs −0.065 and −0.084, so part of the held-out score rewards where people record mosquitoes. Lagged weather adds nothing (+0.008, −0.001).

findings.head: AlphaEarth is the most data-efficient, and sources do not substitute.
findings.body: With 10% of training sites (about 101), AlphaEarth + logistic reaches AP 0.731, matching Environment 41 + RF trained on the same subsets (0.719); it leads at every fraction. Training only on AGES ovitrap detections ranks AGES detections well (AlphaEarth 0.80) but iNaturalist poorly (0.55), and iNaturalist-only training does the reverse. Pooling all sources is best overall.

findings.head: Repeat surveys show detection is not the problem; habitat scores add little within Austria.
findings.body: In 1,641 AGES trap-years (31,972 weekly visits, 2021–2025), per-visit detection is 0.20 and cumulative detection 0.95, so about 5% of occupied trap-years were never detected. No habitat score has an occupancy coefficient whose interval excludes 0. On held-out data the scores lower log-likelihood versus a year-only model, except AlphaEarth + logistic for 2025 (+3.3). At traps new to the network (≥ 1 km from earlier traps), AUC is 0.49–0.60 and every interval includes 0.5.

findings.head: At NEON, habitat scores do predict occupancy, and climate models predict it best.
findings.body: With the NEON token, 42,038 CO2-trap nights at 442 plots (2017–2025) give 3,399 plot-year detection histories for Ae. albopictus. Detection is low (0.12 per night, 0.70 per season), so about 30% of occupied plot-years go undetected. Unlike Austria, every habitat score has a positive occupancy coefficient whose interval excludes 0. Climate 19 BRT, RF and MaxNet rank plots ever detected best (AUC 0.90–0.92) and improve held-out log-likelihood most (+48 to +52 for 2025, about +350 for held-out sites). AlphaEarth + logistic follows (AUC 0.88–0.89), while AlphaEarth RF is near chance (0.54–0.62). Within the 15 sites that had any detection, climate trees still lead (AUC 0.74–0.76) and embeddings fall to 0.47–0.64.

findings.head: The original maps are recovered north of about 6° S and the rebuilt ones match them.
findings.body: The project’s original post-amendment deployment tiles (1,752 of 2,913) reproduce all 12 original surfaces over 5.0 million cells. Rebuilt climate maps agree with them at Pearson 0.986–0.999 and the AlphaEarth overview maps at 0.94–0.97; the refit final models applied to the original cell features agree at 0.96–0.999. Against 1,223 Kraemer et al. (2015) albopictus cells vs random land, the Environment 41 maps score highest (AUC 0.92–0.95), then AlphaEarth (0.90–0.91) and Climate 19 RF (0.87); the order holds 100 km or more from any training site. Human-activity features likely help here because both compendium and iNaturalist records follow people.

findings.head: Dengue: habitat summaries are consistent but small.
findings.body: In a negative-binomial model of monthly municipal dengue cases with a population offset, lagged weather, season and past incidence, both habitat summaries have positive coefficients (Climate 19 RF 0.23, AlphaEarth 0.19 per SD). Forecasting 2024–25 they add +0.0008 to +0.0044 log-likelihood per municipality-month and change deviance by −0.4% to +0.4%. Leaving out each state in turn, they improve log-likelihood in 15–18 of 27 states. On their own they explain little (municipality ρ 0.10–0.17).

findings.head: Supported conclusion.
findings.body: AlphaEarth is the strongest and most data-efficient representation for ranking held-out 2024 blocks, and it beats raw spectra, location encoders and four open S2 foundation models. That advantage does not carry to new years, monitoring networks or disease counts. There, climate models (RF, BRT, R MaxNet) transfer at least as well: they lead on NEON repeat surveys 2017–2025, and outcome-year embeddings make transfer worse. Environment 41 maps lead only on presence-vs-random-land checks, which reward the same human-activity signal as the training data. Use embeddings as a within-distribution ranking tool, not as evidence of better transfer.

notes.maps: Final models refit on all 1,601 sites with the frozen parameters. Climate maps use the original recipe; AlphaEarth maps use the published overview pyramid, which tracks 500 m circle means closely (r ≈ 0.995) but is not identical. Both extrapolate high values into deserts and tropical regions far from any training site. Read colour as rank within one map, not as probability. Environment 41 and fusion surfaces cannot be rebuilt without Earth Engine, so the original surfaces are shown from the recovered deployment tiles (north of about 6° S; parts 18–21 of the Drive archive are not uploaded yet).
notes.p3: Frozen folds, 1,555 sites with every new input (46 primary sites lack Sentinel-2, SatCLIP or weather inputs). Paired 150 km block bootstrap, 1,000 replicates, on pooled out-of-fold scores; about 40 pairs are tested, so treat single borderline intervals with care.
notes.sources: Positives restricted by source in training; the test folds are unchanged. Small numbers after each AP are the same model scored only on iNaturalist presences or only on AGES detections against background.
notes.occupancy: Single-season occupancy per trap-year: ψ from the habitat score (z-scored) plus year; detection from log trap-days, week, week² and NASA POWER mean temperature over the exposure. Intervals: 200 bootstrap replicates over 25 km cells. ΔLL compares held-out log-likelihood with the year-only model; positive is better.
notes.new_locations: First survey year of traps at least 1 or 5 km from every trap in earlier years, pooled 2021–2025, scored with models trained without Austrian rows. Intervals resample 25 km clusters.
notes.p5: Negative-binomial GLM (log link, log-population offset, α profiled). Base: calendar month, NASA POWER temperature, rain and humidity lagged 1–2 months, 12-month mean temperature, log population density and log incidence lagged 1 and 12 months. Cases are InfoDengue/Mosqlimate municipal counts; habitat summaries average the frozen 2024 maps over each municipality. Disease counts were never used as mosquito labels. GLM intervals ignore spatial clustering, so the state-level results are the better guide.
notes.neon: Occupancy per plot-year (≥ 2 trap nights): ψ from year and the habitat score; detection from log trap hours, day of year and its square. Intervals: 100 bootstrap replicates over the 44 NEON sites. ΔLL compares held-out log-likelihood with the year-only model (positive is better): 2025 from 2017–2024 fits, and 5-fold held-out NEON sites. “Refit” scores use the final models on WorldClim and AlphaEarth features at the plot; “original map” scores sample the project’s own 0.05° surfaces. No NEON record is in the training cohort.
notes.kraemer: Kraemer et al. (2015) Ae. albopictus point records 1960–2014 (Dryad, CC0; Zenodo mirror with matching checksum), one per 0.05° cell, vs 50,000 random cells from the area every surface covers. This scores presence against random land, not absence, and the compendium is not a systematic survey. Intervals: 500 bootstrap replicates over 5° blocks.
notes.year: Same 2024-trained models; test-site features taken from the 2024 or the 2025 embedding at the same 500 m support. TESSERA 2025 tiles are partial on the public mirror (337 of 389 NEON sites), so its paired difference uses the shared sites only. R MaxNet rows compare with the Python elapid stand-in on the same 2024 features.
